newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Africa Israel rated buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Africa Israel rated buy.

text.p: Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull Securities rated Africa Israel Investments a buy, saying the shares are undervalued despite a recent rally.

"The 50 percent stake in Migdal, the leading insurance group in Israel with 24 percent of the market, is now known to be worth $500 million, which highlights just how cheap the shares still are," analyst Keith Phillips said in a report.
Africa Israel's insurance holdings will be spun off and quoted on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, after which Italian insurer Generali will take control of Migdal.

Africa's parent company Bank Leumi plans to issue a tender shortly to sell off part of its shares in Africa to comply with Israeli banking law. Leumi owns 65 percent of Africa and must reduce this stake to 25 percent.
Both these factors sparked a recent rally in Africa shares.

"Despite the recent rally, the shares have fallen back and are well off their high and well below their true value," the report said. "In our view the company should be valued at $900 million. Currently the market capitalisation is only $573 million."
The company's earnings per shares will rise to an estimated 280.07 shekels in 1996 and 344.45 shekels in 1997 from 223.27 in 1995.
The company is one of Israel's leading conglomerates, with interests in construction, property leasing, hotels and insurance.
